results.title: Class functions on a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a set. A function $f : G \to k$ is a class function when it is constant on conjugacy classes, that is, $f(h g h^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$.

results.title: The space of class functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. The space of class functions $G \to k$ is the $k$-linear subspace of the vector space of all functions $G \to k$, under pointwise addition and scalar multiplication, consisting of the class functions.

results.title: Characters are class functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For every finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ over $k$, the character of $V$, the function sending $g \in G$ to the trace of the linear map by which $g$ acts on $V$, is a class function on $G$.

results.title: Class functions agree on conjugate elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $f : G \to k$ be a class function with values in a set $k$. If $x, y \in G$ are conjugate, then $f(x) = f(y)$.

results.title: Class functions factor through conjugacy classes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a set, and write $[x]$ for the conjugacy class of $x \in G$. A function $f : G \to k$ is a class function if and only if there is a function $q$ from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ such that $f(x) = q([x])$ for all $x \in G$.

results.title: Class functions as functions on conjugacy classes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field, and write $[x]$ for the conjugacy class of $x \in G$. This is the $k$-linear isomorphism from the space of class functions $G \to k$ to the vector space of all functions from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ that sends a class function $f$ to the function $[x] \mapsto f(x)$; its inverse sends a function $q$ on conjugacy classes to the class function $x \mapsto q([x])$.

results.title: Evaluating a class function on conjugacy classes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For every class function $f : G \to k$ and every $x \in G$, the function on conjugacy classes that corresponds to $f$ under the linear isomorphism between class functions and functions on conjugacy classes takes the value $f(x)$ at the conjugacy class of $x$.

results.title: Lifting a function on conjugacy classes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For every function $q$ from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ and every $x \in G$, the class function that corresponds to $q$ under the inverse of the linear isomorphism between class functions and functions on conjugacy classes takes at $x$ the value of $q$ at the conjugacy class of $x$.

results.title: Dimension of the space of class functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $k$ a field. The space of class functions $G \to k$ is a $k$-vector space whose dimension equals the number of conjugacy classes of $G$.

results.title: Irreducible representations are simple objects
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a field, $G$ a group and $\rho$ an irreducible representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$. Then $\rho$, viewed as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over $k$, is a simple object.

results.title: Characters of nonisomorphic simple representations are linearly independent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $(V_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ such that $V_i \cong V_j$ implies $i = j$. Then the characters of the $V_i$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Irreducible characters are linearly independent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. The irreducible complex characters of $G$, that is, the functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$ that are the character of some simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$, are linearly independent over $\mathbb{C}$ in the space of functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Irreducible characters span the class functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $f(hgh^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$. Then $f$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-linear combination of irreducible complex characters of $G$, that is, of functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$ that are the character of some simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$.

results.title: Number of irreducible characters
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. The number of irreducible complex characters of $G$, that is, of functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$ that are the character of some simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$, equals the number of conjugacy classes of $G$.

results.title: Involution-generated 2-groups with the Engel condition on involutions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has this property when every element of $G$ has order a power of $2$, $G$ is generated by its involutions, and $[[x, u], u] = 1$ for every $x \in G$ and every involution $u \in G$, where $[x, u] = x^{-1} u^{-1} x u$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 18.57 on the derived length of involution-generated 2-groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition (Kourovka 18.57, D. V. Lytkina) that there is a natural number $d$ such that $G^{(d)} = 1$ for every finite group $G$ in which every element has order a power of $2$, which is generated by its involutions, and in which $[[x, u], u] = 1$ for every $x \in G$ and every involution $u \in G$; here $[x, u] = x^{-1} u^{-1} x u$ and $G^{(d)}$ is the $d$-th term of the derived series of $G$.

results.title: Negative answer to Kourovka Problem 18.57
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is no natural number $d$ such that $G^{(d)} = 1$ for every finite group $G$ in which every element has order a power of $2$, which is generated by its involutions, and in which $[[x, u], u] = 1$ for every $x \in G$ and every involution $u \in G$; here $[x, u] = x^{-1} u^{-1} x u$ and $G^{(d)}$ is the $d$-th term of the derived series of $G$. Thus the derived length of such groups is unbounded.

results.title: Even-index Euler numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The integers $E_0, E_2, E_4, \dots$ defined recursively by $E_0 = 1$ and $E_{2m} = -\sum_{k=0}^{m-1} \binom{2m}{2k} E_{2k}$ for $m \ge 1$; equivalently, $\sum_{k=0}^{m} \binom{2m}{2k} E_{2k}$ is $1$ for $m = 0$ and $0$ for $m \ge 1$. The value at $n$ is $E_{2n}$.

results.title: Recursion for the even-index Euler numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m \ge 1$, $E_{2m} = -\sum_{k=0}^{m-1} \binom{2m}{2k} E_{2k}$.

results.title: Binomial recurrence for the even-index Euler numbers

results.title: Bernoulli numbers as a convolution of even-index Euler numbers
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Termwise bound for the Clausen series (Chapter 9, Entry 13)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $k$ and a real number $x$, let $t_k = \sin((k+1)x)/(k+1)^m$ if $m$ is even and $t_k = \cos((k+1)x)/(k+1)^m$ if $m$ is odd. Then $\lvert t_k\rvert \le 1/(k+1)^m$.

results.title: Summability of the Clausen series (Chapter 9, Entry 13)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m \ge 2$ and every real $x$, the series $\sum_{k \ge 1} \sin(kx)/k^m$ (if $m$ is even) or $\sum_{k \ge 1} \cos(kx)/k^m$ (if $m$ is odd) is summable.

results.title: Clausen function of order zero (Chapter 9, Entry 13)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Clausen-type functions $C_m$ of Entry 13 are defined by $C_1(x) = -\log\lvert 2\sin(x/2)\rvert$ and, for $m \ge 2$, $C_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} \sin(kx)/k^m$ for even $m$ and $C_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} \cos(kx)/k^m$ for odd $m$, together with the convention $C_0 = 0$: for every real $x$, $C_0(x) = 0$.

results.title: Clausen function of order one (Chapter 9, Entry 13)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The order-one Clausen-type function $C_1$ of Entry 13 is the log-sine function: for every real $x$, $C_1(x) = -\log\lvert 2\sin(x/2)\rvert$, with the convention $\log 0 = 0$, so that $C_1$ vanishes at the integer multiples of $2\pi$.

results.title: Clausen functions of order at least two as series (Chapter 9, Entry 13)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C_m$ be the Clausen-type function of Entry 13, with $C_0 = 0$ and $C_1(x) = -\log\lvert 2\sin(x/2)\rvert$. For every natural number $m \ge 2$ and every real $x$, $C_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} \sin(kx)/k^m$ if $m$ is even and $C_m(x) = \sum_{k \ge 1} \cos(kx)/k^m$ if $m$ is odd.

results.title: Strict growth of a set of generators
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $F$ of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ has strict growth when $x < f(x)$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Self-generating sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. A set $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is self-generating for $s$ and $F$ when $s \in \Gamma$ and $f(x) \in \Gamma$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \Gamma$.

results.title: Fixed-point sets for a seed and generators
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. A set $C \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a fixed-point set for $F$ and $s$ when, for every $y \in \mathbb{N}$, $y \in C$ if and only if $y = s$ or $y = f(x)$ for some $f \in F$ and some $x \in C$; equivalently, $C = \{s\} \cup \bigcup_{f \in F} f(C)$.

results.title: Reachability from a seed by generators
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. Reachability from $s$ is the least predicate on $\mathbb{N}$ that holds at $s$ and holds at $f(w)$ whenever it holds at $w$ and $f \in F$. Thus $y$ is reachable exactly when $y = f_k(\cdots f_1(s) \cdots)$ for some $k \ge 0$ and $f_1, \ldots, f_k \in F$; the case $k = 0$ is $s$ itself.

results.title: Set generated from a seed
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $F$ of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a seed $s \in \mathbb{N}$, the set generated from $s$ by $F$ consists of all numbers $f_k(\cdots f_1(s) \cdots)$ with $k \ge 0$ and $f_1, \dots, f_k \in F$; the case $k = 0$ gives $s$ itself.

results.title: Fixed-point sets are self-generating
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$. Every fixed-point set $C$ for $F$ and $s$ is self-generating: $s \in C$, and $f(x) \in C$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in C$.

results.title: The generated set is self-generating
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$. The set generated from $s$ by $F$ contains $s$ and is closed under every $f \in F$: if $x$ is in it and $f \in F$, then $f(x)$ is in it.

results.title: The generated set lies in every self-generating set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. If a set $G \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contains $s$ and satisfies $f(x) \in G$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in G$, then $G$ contains the set generated from $s$ by $F$, that is, every number obtained from $s$ by applying finitely many (possibly no) functions of $F$ in succession.

results.title: The generated set is the intersection of all self-generating sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $s \in \mathbb{N}$. The set generated from $s$ by $F$ equals the intersection of all sets $G \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contain $s$ and are closed under every $f \in F$.

results.title: Under strict growth, a fixed-point set is the intersection of all self-generating sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $x < f(x)$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. If $C$ is a fixed-point set for $F$ and $s$, then $C$ is the intersection of all sets $G \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contain $s$ and are closed under every $f \in F$.

results.title: Under strict growth, a fixed-point set is the least self-generating set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $x < f(x)$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. If $C$ is a fixed-point set for $F$ and $s$, then $C$ contains $s$ and is closed under every $f \in F$, and $C \subseteq G$ for every set $G \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contains $s$ and is closed under every $f \in F$.

results.title: The least self-generating set is the generated set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. Call a set $G \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ self-generating if $s \in G$ and $f(x) \in G$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in G$. If $C$ is self-generating and is contained in every self-generating set, then $C$ equals the set generated from $s$ by $F$.

results.title: Under strict growth, fixed-point sets are unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $x < f(x)$ for every $f \in F$ and every $x \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $s \in \mathbb{N}$. If $C_1$ and $C_2$ are both fixed-point sets for $F$ and $s$, then $C_1 = C_2$.

results.title: Balanced endpoint ownership
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Every owned role has its opposite role at the same physical name, with the same rank and the dual protocol. This condition may permit deadlocks.

results.title: The empty interface is balanced

results.title: A fresh restriction pair is balanced

results.title: Rekeying preserves balance
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Compatibility of a partial endpoint interface

results.title: Mutual information of a finite joint law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Mutual information `I(X; Y)` of a finite joint law `p` of `(X, Y)`, in bits: the real value of `measureMutualInformation` on `p`, which is finite here (`finiteMutualInformation_eq`). Each finite alphabet carries the discrete σ-algebra.

results.title: Mutual information in terms of entropies
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `I(X; Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X, Y)` for a finite joint law.

results.title: Conditional mutual information of a finite joint law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conditional mutual information `I(X; Y | Z)` of a finite joint law `p` of `(X, Y, Z)`, in bits: `∑ p(x, y, z) log₂ (p(x, y, z) p(z) / (p(x, z) p(y, z)))`.

results.title: Conditional mutual information in terms of entropies
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `I(X; Y | Z) = H(X, Z) + H(Y, Z) - H(X, Y, Z) - H(Z)`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of conditional mutual information
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Conditional mutual information is nonnegative.

results.title: Vanishing conditional mutual information iff conditional independence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `I(X; Y | Z) = 0` exactly when `X` and `Y` are conditionally independent given `Z`: `p(x, y, z) p(z) = p(x, z) p(y, z)` for every atom.

results.title: Chain rule for mutual information
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `I(X; (Y, Z)) = I(X; Z) + I(X; Y | Z)`. Here `p` is read as a joint law of `X` and the pair `(Y, Z)`.

results.title: Data-processing inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Data-processing inequality, first half: if `X` and `Z` are conditionally independent given `Y` (a Markov chain `X - Y - Z`, stated as `I(X; Z | Y) = 0` for the joint law `p` of `(X, Y, Z)`), then `I(X; Z) ≤ I(X; Y)`.

results.title: Data-processing inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Data-processing inequality, second half: under the same Markov condition, `I(X; Z) ≤ I(Y; Z)`.
